properties.description:
* WHAT...High Rip Current Risk, life-threatening rip current.

* WHERE...From Rincon to Fajardo

* WHEN...Through Saturday afternoon

* IMPACTS...Rip currents can sweep even the best swimmers away
from shore into deeper water, where it becomes difficult to
return to safety.
properties.instruction:
There is a high risk of rip currents.

Rip currents are powerful channels of water flowing quickly away
from shore, which occur most often at low spots or breaks in the
sandbar and in the vicinity of structures such as groins, jetties
and piers. Heed the advice of lifeguards, beach patrol flags and
signs.

If you become caught in a rip current, yell for help. Remain
calm, do not exhaust yourself and stay afloat while waiting for
help. If you have to swim out of a rip current, swim parallel to
shore and back toward the beach when possible. Do not attempt to
swim directly against a rip current as you will tire quickly.

properties.headline: Coastal Flood Advisory issued November 20 at 12:14PM PST until November 25 at 3:00AM PST by NWS Los Angeles/Oxnard CA
properties.description:
* WHAT...For the Beach Hazards Statement, dangerous rip currents
and breaking waves due to elevated surf. Elevated to high surf
will likely continue into much of next week. For the Coastal
Flood Advisory, moderate coastal flooding expected. For the
Coastal Flood Watch, significant coastal flooding possible.

* WHERE...Malibu Coast and Los Angeles County Beaches.Impacts
highest across west-facing beaches, including from Santa Monica
to Palos Verdes. In addition, the Long Beach/Naples area will be
susceptible to the very high water levels.

* WHEN...For the Beach Hazards Statement, until 3 PM PST this
afternoon. For the Coastal Flood Advisory, from 3 AM Monday to
3 AM PST Wednesday. For the Coastal Flood Watch, from late
Tuesday night through Thursday afternoon.

* IMPACTS...There is a moderate risk for damaging flooding of
sea water over some vulnerable low-lying coastal areas,
especially around the time of high tide, including over
beaches, roads, and structures. Significant beach erosion is
possible. There is an increased risk of ocean drowning. Rip
currents can pull swimmers and surfers out to sea. Waves can
wash people off beaches and rocks, and capsize small boats
nearshore.

* ADDITIONAL DETAILS...Highest risk likely Wednesday and Thursday
with potential for significant impacts. Additional products
will likely be needed into Friday.
.
properties.instruction:
Take the necessary actions to protect flood-prone property. Plan
for extra travel time as some roads may be closed.

Remain out of the water due to hazardous swimming conditions, or
stay near occupied lifeguard towers. Rock jetties can be deadly
in such conditions, stay off the rocks.

properties.headline: Flood Warning issued November 20 at 2:17PM EST until November 22 at 9:00AM EST by NWS Jacksonville FL
properties.description:
...The National Weather Service in Jacksonville has issued a Flood
Warning for the following rivers in Florida...

North Fork Black Creek At Middleburg affecting Clay County.

Additional information is available at
https://water.weather.gov/wfo/JAX

The next statement will be issued Saturday afternoon at 230 PM EST.

* WHAT...Minor flooding is forecast.

* WHERE...North Fork Black Creek at Middleburg.

* WHEN...From Saturday afternoon to Sunday morning.

* IMPACTS...At 13.0 feet, Water begins to flood wooded areas along
portions of North Fork Black Creek downstream from the gage to near
Blanding Blvd. At 15.0 feet, Water begins to enter backyards of
residential properties along Hawk Haven Road and Lazy Acres Road
and Redbug Alley on the north bank of the North Fork. Flooding
begins at Enchanted Lane on the south bank of the North Fork. At
16.0 feet, Flooding expands into the yards of more properties along
Lazy Acres Road on the north bank of the North Fork. Flooding
begins further downstream of the Blanding Blvd Bridge along North
and South Lee. Flooding begins on areas of the south bank of the
North Fork, particularly at Scenic Drive and Enchanted Lane.

* ADDITIONAL DETAILS...
- At 1:00 PM EST Friday the stage was 3.0 feet.
- Forecast...The river is expected to rise above flood stage early
tomorrow afternoon to a crest of 15.3 feet tomorrow evening. It
will then fall below flood stage early Sunday morning.
- Flood stage is 15.0 feet.
- http://www.weather.gov/safety/flood

unknown depth. Take the necessary actions to protect flood-prone
property.
